title: Reinstatement of a Defaulted Plan: Window and Count
content:
**Revenue Cycle Policy Manual — Patient Payment Plans: reinstatement of a defaulted plan**

**R1. Count.** A defaulted plan can be reinstated only while its reinstatement count is below the term's number of reinstatements allowed. The reinstatement count is the number of times the plan has already been reinstated, as the plan record shows.

**R2. Window.** Reinstatement is possible only within the term's reinstatement window, in calendar days, after the default date. The reinstatement window counts calendar days with the default date as day 0, and a reinstatement on the last day is on time. The default date is the date recorded on the plan when it defaulted.

**R3. Payment of missed installments — no longer in force.** The former clause that the patient must first pay every missed installment in full is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the payment made on a defaulted plan.

**R4. Re-enrollment on the original schedule — no longer in force.** The former clause that on reinstatement the balances released at default are enrolled again on the same plan from the invoices that are still open, with the original schedule, and that the invoices leave the statement cycle again, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for re-enrollment and the installment of a reinstated plan.

**R5. Invoices in collections.** An invoice placed in collections since the default is not re-enrolled.

## Window boundary cases (hypothetical default on 10 March)

| Window | Last day on time | Reinstatement on that day | Reinstatement the day after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days | 9 April (day 30) | On time | Outside the window |
| 45 days | 24 April (day 45) | On time | Outside the window |

## Count and window together

| Reinstatement count below the allowance | Within the window | Reinstatement possible |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | No | No |
| No | Yes | No |
| No | No | No |

A term whose allowance is 0 can never meet R1, so a plan on that term is never reinstated.

superseded_clauses: The patient must first pay every missed installment in full;

on reinstatement the balances released at default are enrolled again on the same plan from the invoices that are still open, with the original schedule, and the invoices leave the statement cycle again.
